who: Richard Eugene Sullivan, medieval historian at Michigan State University, PhD Illinois 1949.

evidence.says: MSU oral history, pp. 2–6: Sullivan describes graduate study in medieval history at Illinois, completing his doctorate in spring 1949, and joining Michigan State in 1954.
Richard E. (Richard Eugene) Sullivan is identified through Carolingian Missionary Activity, 690–814; another source explicitly identifies him with Michigan State University.
The Richard James Sullivan record identifies a Federal Reserve economist with an economics PhD from Illinois-Urbana and cites his 1983 Illinois dissertation.

notes: The medieval field, MSU appointment and 1949 Illinois doctorate identify Richard Eugene Sullivan. The alternative Illinois doctorate belongs to a different person and period.

who: Lewis A. Erenberg, historian of US social and cultural history at Loyola University Chicago, PhD Michigan 1974.

evidence.says: Lewis A. Erenberg’s institutional CV lists a history PhD from Michigan in 1974 and Loyola appointments beginning in 1976.
Loyola names Lewis Erenberg as dissertation director for Kevin Kaufmann’s Rigorous Honesty, Ronald Martin’s Flowers in Chicago, and Cord Scott’s Comics and Conflict.
The Lewis A. Erenberg authority cites Loyola’s faculty biography, identifying its historian who taught there in 1976–2009.

notes: Degree and direct student-supervisor evidence agree. Loyola lists Kaufmann under 2011, whereas the supplied AHA record says 2012; the dissertation title and advisor agree.

who: Joseph T. Glatthaar, military and Civil War historian at UNC Chapel Hill, PhD Wisconsin-Madison 1983.

evidence.says: The Society for Military History’s Winter 2009 biography identifies Joseph T. Glatthaar as UNC Chapel Hill’s Stephenson Distinguished Professor and gives his Wisconsin-Madison PhD as 1983.
Ohio Wesleyan’s October 2019 lecture announcement identifies Glatthaar as UNC Chapel Hill’s distinguished history professor and lists The March to the Sea and Beyond among his books.
The Joseph T. Glatthaar authority identifies him as author of The March to the Sea and Beyond and The American Military.

notes: Candidate authority, military-history works, UNC affiliation during the student period and doctoral institution/year agree.

who: Kathryn M. McPherson, historian of women, gender and nursing at York University, PhD Simon Fraser.

evidence.says: York identifies Kathryn M. McPherson as a history professor with a Simon Fraser PhD and lists her book Bedside Matters: The Transformation of Canadian Nursing, 1900–1990.
York’s May 2015 teaching-award announcement identifies McPherson as a history professor who had supervised thirteen completed PhDs, with six more in progress.
The authority for Kathryn McPherson cites Bedside Matters (1996), identifying its author as an associate professor of history at York University.

notes: Authority, book, York affiliation and doctoral institution agree. The selected faculty biography does not supply a doctorate year.

who: Philip G. Nord, historian of modern France at Princeton University, PhD Columbia 1982.

evidence.says: Nord’s institutional CV lists Columbia PhD 1982 and continuous Princeton history appointments from 1981 through the CV’s date.
Princeton’s faculty account identifies his modern French history field and describes his supervision of doctoral dissertations, including French aviation history.
The authority identifies Philip G. Nord through Paris Shopkeepers and the Politics of Resentment and explicitly places him in Princeton’s history department.

notes: The exact Columbia degree/year, Princeton career and French-history works identify the candidate.

who: Randy W. Roberts, historian of US sport and popular culture at Purdue University, PhD Louisiana State 1978.

evidence.says: Purdue identifies Randy W. Roberts as a distinguished history professor, lists Louisiana State PhD 1978, and gives sports history and popular culture among his specialties.
Purdue’s account says Roberts arrived in 1988 and identifies him as John Matthew Smith’s Purdue advisor.
The authority identifies Randy W. Roberts with Purdue University and describes him as a history professor and author of sports-history books.

notes: Degree/year, Purdue career, sports-history field and direct evidence for listed student John Smith agree.

who: Michael McCormick, medieval historian at Harvard University, doctorate Université catholique de Louvain 1979.

evidence.says: Harvard identifies McCormick as Francis Goelet Professor of Medieval History, with a Louvain PhD and a Harvard appointment beginning in 1991; it lists Origins of the European Economy among his works.
The American Philosophical Society’s 2021 biography dates his Louvain doctorate to 1979 and confirms his Harvard appointment from 1991.
The authority identifies the author of Origins of the European Economy with Harvard University and links him to Eternal Victory.

notes: Louvain doctorate, Harvard career and medieval-history works agree with the candidate authority.

who: Paul Jankowski, historian of modern France and European warfare at Brandeis University, doctorate Oxford.

evidence.says: Brandeis identifies Jankowski as Raymond Ginger Professor Emeritus of History, specializing in modern Europe, France and warfare, and lists his doctorate from Oxford.
The 2005 Brandeis faculty profile identifies Paul Jankowski as its Ray Ginger Professor and history department chair, with BA and PhD from Oxford and research on modern France.
The authority explicitly cites the Brandeis faculty guide identifying Paul Jankowski as Raymond Ginger Professor of History; it links him to Communism and Collaboration.

notes: Oxford doctorate, Brandeis appointment and modern French history field agree with the candidate authority.
